title: October 2024 STM Warrant
text: THE COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS SPECIAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT TOWN OF NORWOOD Norfolk, ss. To either of the Constables in the Town of Norwood in said County, Greetings: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby required to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Norwood, qualified as the law requires to vote in Town affairs, to meet in the Norwood High School Auditorium at 245 Nichols Street in said Town on Thursday, October 24, 2024, at 6:30 o’clock in the afternoon to meet and act at said time and place on the following Articles: ARTICLE 1: To see what sum of money the Town will vote to transfer from surplus revenue or other available funds and appropriate to purchase and implement a Police Department body-worn camera system, including all associated costs; or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 2: To see what sum of money the Town will vote to transfer from surplus revenue or other available funds and appropriate to the stabilization fund; or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 3: To see what sum of money the Town will vote to transfer from surplus revenue or other available funds and appropriate to the compensated absences fund; or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 4. To see what sum ‘or sums of money the Town will vote to transfer from surplus revenue or other available funds, or borrow, and to appropriate for the costs of capital projects, including construction, reconstruction and major renovations and repairs to buildings, facilities, and other public works; the purchase of new equipment; and engineering, design and other costs incidental and related to such capital projects; and for other capital projects not otherwise specified. And further, to see if the Town will vote to authorize the Treasurer with the approval of the Board of Selectmen to borrow said sums required by the aforesaid capital projects; and to authorize the Board of Selectmen to expend the aforesaid funds for the specified purposes; or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 5. To see what sum of money the Town will vote to transfer and appropriate from the Community Preservation Fund, from surplus revenue, or from other available funds, for the following purpose: to fund purchase of land with buildings thereon and development of approximately 20 units of affordable housing for income qualified veterans of U.S. Military service with deed restrictions in perpetuity, located at 20 Vernon Street, Norwood, to be administered by Caritas Communities, a Massachusetts non-profit corporation in accordance with the terms of a Grant Agreement and Security Agreement between the Town and Caritas Communities, and to authorize the Town to execute all necessary and appropriate instruments related thereto; or take any other action in the matter. (On petition of the Community Preservation Committee) ARTICLE 6: ARTICLE 7: To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Board of Selectmen to grant to Verizon New England, Inc., upon such terms as the Board of Selectmen shall determine, an easement which would allow installation and maintenance of a pole and related equipment on the site of the new Coakley Middle School described as 1271 and 1315 Washington Street, Norwood, MA, for the purpose of transmission and distribution of telecommunication. The location of the proposed Easement Area is shown on a plan, a copy of which is on file in the office of the Town Clerk; or take any other action in the matter. To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Board of Selectmen to petition the General Court to enact legislation in substantially the following form, which would amend the provisions of Chapter 81 of the Acts of 2010, AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE APPOINTMENT OF RETIRED POLICE OFFICERS AS SPECIAL POLICE OFFICERS IN THE TOWN OF NORWOOD by removing in Section | the restriction on hiring only retired Norwood police officers and allowing the general manager to appoint police officers who retired in good standing from a Massachusetts community based upon superannuation; provided that the General Court may reasonably vary the form and substance of the requested legislation within the scope of the general public objectives of the petition. As amended, the first sentence of said Section 1 would read as follows: The general manager of the town of Norwood may appoint, as he deems necessary, retired police officers from a Massachusetts community as special police officers for the purpose of performing police details or any other police duties arising therefrom or during the course of police detail work, whether or not related to the detail work; provided however that such retired police officers shall have been regular police officers who retired in good standing from a Massachusetts community based upon superannuation; or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 8. To see if the Town, pursuant to M.G.L. Chapter 98, Section 56, will vote to establish a General Bylaw by adding an Article which will establish all or some of the fees sealers shall receive and inspectors may demand for sealing and inspecting the weighing or measuring devices set forth below; or take any other action in the matter. Sealer of Weights and Measures 1. Other Devices Taxi Meter : $40.00 Odometer - Hubodometer $40.00 Leather Meas. (Semi-Annual) $20.00 Fabric Measuring $20.00 Wire-Rope Cordage $20.00 6. Scanners 3 or less $75.00 4 to 10 Registers $150.00 more than 11 $250.00 7. Linear Measure Yard Sticks $5.00 Tapes $15.00 8. Miscellaneous Milk bottles or jars $20.00 Dry Measures $5.00 Reverse Vending Machine $25.00 Scale Calibration ARTICLE 9: Cost of Device Test To see if the Town will vote to accept M.G.L. c. 64N Section 3(a) and impose a local sales tax upon the sale of marijuana or marijuana products by a vendor operating within the Town at a rate of 3% of the total sale price received by the vendor from the sale of marijuana, or marijuana products, said excise to take effect on the first day of the calendar quarter commencing at least thirty days after such vote of Town Meeting; or take any other action in the matter. Any individual with a disability who needs accommodations related to accessibility/communications or other aspects of participation in Town Meeting or other related programs should contact: Tony Mazzucco General Manager Town of Norwood 566 Washington Street Norwood, MA 02062 The Town of Norwood does not discriminate on the basis of disability. And you are directed to serve this warrant by posting attested copies thereof in ten public places in this Town fourteen days at least before the time and day of said meeting. Hereof fail not and make due return of this warrant with your doings thereon to the Selectmen on or before the day and time of said meeting. Given under our hands at Norwood this twenty-fourth day of September, A.D. 2024. Robert G. Donnelly, Chairm: a Grow, Vi 5 PE SA a atthew E. = , a 7 Michget Sad I SELECTMEN OF NORWOOD
